description: Solo project building a browser-based lunar and Martian habitat simulator for students. Focuses on life support (ECLSS), power systems, and resource management using real NASA datasets. Team is closed.
summary:
Outpost One: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based space habitat simulator designed for students ages 7–12 to experience the real engineering trade-offs of deep-space survival. Acting as Base Commanders at Shackleton Crater on the Moon or Jezero Crater on Mars, players deploy modular infrastructure—including solar arrays, Li-ion batteries, Kilopower reactors, Sabatier/MOXIE oxygen units, hydroponic greenhouses, and sintered regolith radiation domes—across a grid while managing finite credits and interdependent life-support systems.

Traditional STEM materials often oversimplify mission planning or overwhelm young learners with dense technical jargon. Outpost One bridges this gap through cause-and-effect gameplay grounded in real NASA science, incorporating Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) closed-loop math, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) polar conditions, MOXIE oxygen extraction principles, Space Weather Database (DONKI) solar particle events, and Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) astronaut health baselines. Instead of punitive game-over screens, an integrated Flight Director AI explains failures using plain-language physics. By making complex resource budgeting accessible in a zero-install web app, Outpost One inspires young learners to think like real NASA mission planners.
details: Outpost One: Junior Mission Trainer is an interactive web-based space habitat and Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) simulator built using HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript (hosted at https://hari13022.github.io/outpost-one/). Designed for aspiring junior astronauts and STEM learners, the game challenges players to sustain a 4-person Artemis crew across 15 Sols at Moon (Shackleton Crater) and Mars (Jezero Crater). How It Works & Key Features: - Real-Time Closed-Loop ECLSS Physics: Players balance continuous production against crew consumption across five interdependent survival systems—Power Grid (kW/kWh), Cabin Oxygen (kg/h), Water Reserve (recycling efficiency & net flow), Food & Hydroponics (rations & fresh yield), and Radiation Shielding (% protected). - Modular Surface Outpost Grid: Using Construct Credits (CC), players construct and manage Solar Arrays, Li-Ion Battery Banks, Kilopower Reactors, Sabatier/MOXIE O₂ extractors, Hydroponic Greenhouses, and Regolith Radiation Domes while adapting to planetary day/night cycles, surface temperatures (-120°C), and Earth communication delays (1.3s Moon LOS). - NASA Flight Director AI & Directives: Instead of punitive game-over screens, an integrated Flight Director AI explains system bottlenecks using plain-language physics alongside live crew status logs and surface survey directives.
